hints.title: Inflection Point Detection
hints.text: In an array rotated between 1 and n times, one half is always strictly sorted while the other half contains the inflection point. How can comparing the middle element with the rightmost element locate the minimum?

hints.title: Right Boundary Comparison
hints.text: If nums[mid] > nums[right], the minimum resides strictly to the right of mid. If nums[mid] <= nums[right], the minimum is at mid or to its left.

hints.title: Rotated Range Reduction
hints.text: Initialize left = 0 and right = len(nums) - 1. While left < right, compute mid. If nums[mid] > nums[right], the pivot lies right, so set left = mid + 1. Otherwise set right = mid. When left == right, return nums[left].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 5000)
complexity.notes: Halves the search interval on each step by comparing with rightmost element.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear scan takes O(N) time. The problem specifically asks for an algorithm that runs in O(log N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Logarithmic O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space by comparing against nums[right].
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clear explanation of why comparing nums[mid] to nums[right] works (and why comparing to nums[left] is ambiguous for unrotated arrays), loop condition left < right, and convergence on the minimum.

solutions.approach: Iterative Pivot Elimination with Right Boundary
